subject: biochemistry
title: Inborn errors of amino acid metabolism: PKU, alkaptonuria, MSUD and homocystinuria

steps.tx: **Phenylketonuria (PKU)** is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by deficient **phenylalanine hydroxylase** or its cofactor tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4). Phenylalanine accumulates and diverts into phenylpyruvate, phenylacetate, and phenyllactate. Untreated children develop profound intellectual disability, microcephaly, seizures, hypopigmentation from reduced melanin, and a characteristic **mousy or musty body odour**. Management requires dietary phenylalanine restriction and tyrosine supplementation initiated immediately after newborn screening.
steps.say: Phenylketonuria results from phenylalanine hydroxylase or BH4 deficiency. Toxic phenylketones accumulate, causing severe mental disability, seizures, fair skin, and a musty body odour. Early dietary phenylalanine restriction combined with tyrosine supplementation prevents neurological damage.

steps.tx: **Alkaptonuria** is a benign-appearing autosomal recessive disorder caused by deficiency of **homogentisate 1,2-dioxygenase** in the tyrosine degradation pathway. Homogentisic acid accumulates and oxidizes to a dark polymer. Hallmarks include urine that **turns black upon standing or alkalinization**, dark blue-black pigment deposition in connective tissues (**ochronosis**), scleral pigmentation, and debilitating degenerative arthritis of large joints and the spine in adulthood.
steps.say: Alkaptonuria involves homogentisate dioxygenase deficiency in tyrosine breakdown. Accumulating homogentisic acid oxidizes to black pigment. Patients have urine that darkens when exposed to air, blue-black scleral pigmentation, and severe ochronotic osteoarthritis in later life.

rows: Homogentisic acid auto-oxidation in alkaline air

steps.tx: **Maple syrup urine disease (MSUD)** results from deficiency of the mitochondrial **branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase** complex, which requires thiamine, lipoic acid, CoA, FAD, and NAD. Leucine, isoleucine, and valine and their respective alpha-ketoacids accumulate to neurotoxic levels. Neonates present within the first week of life with poor feeding, vomiting, lethargy, alternating hypertonia and hypotonia, cerebral oedema, and a **sweet maple syrup or burnt sugar odour** in urine and earwax.
steps.say: Maple syrup urine disease is caused by branched chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase deficiency. Leucine, isoleucine, and valine build up, causing neonatal vomiting, encephalopathy, seizures, and a sweet maple syrup smell in urine. Dietary restriction of branched chain amino acids is life saving.

nodes.label: Accumulation of branched amino acids and ketoacids
Encephalopathy, cerebral oedema, burnt sugar urine odour

steps.tx: Classical **homocystinuria** is an autosomal recessive deficiency of **cystathionine beta-synthase (CBS)**, requiring pyridoxal phosphate (vitamin B6). Homocysteine accumulates while cysteine becomes essential. Clinical features include Marfanoid habitus, osteoporosis, downward and inward **ectopia lentis** (subluxation of the lens), intellectual disability, and premature **thromboembolism** in arteries and veins. Treatment involves high-dose vitamin B6 in responsive patients, dietary methionine restriction, cysteine supplementation, and betaine.
steps.say: Classical homocystinuria is caused by cystathionine beta synthase deficiency. Patients present with a Marfanoid habitus, downward lens dislocation, mental disability, and severe early arterial and venous thrombosis. Vitamin B6, methionine restriction, and betaine form standard therapy.

steps.tx: The urea cycle disposes of waste nitrogen by converting ammonia to urea in hepatocytes. **Ornithine transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency** is the most common urea cycle disorder and the only X-linked one. Excess carbamoyl phosphate leaks into the cytoplasm, driving pyrimidine synthesis and causing massive **orotic aciduria**. Neonates develop lethargy, hypothermia, tachypnoea from respiratory alkalosis, and cerebral oedema. Elevated blood ammonia with high urinary orotate confirms OTC deficiency over carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I deficiency.
steps.say: The urea cycle eliminates ammonia as urea. Ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency is the only X linked urea cycle defect. Excess carbamoyl phosphate spills into pyrimidine synthesis, causing massive urinary orotic acid and life threatening hyperammonaemic encephalopathy.
